report.scanSummary: I checked the week 38 zero-touch rate (14–20 Sep) for every managed-service customer against its 40.0% XLA target. Two customers fell below it, for two very different reasons.

items.title: Fabrikam Industries — 34.0% zero-touch (target 40.0%)
items.quote: 51 of 150 tickets resolved with no human touch, down from 46.0% (23 of 50) the week before.
items.note: The ontology ties the drop to MI-FAB-0001 (Sev2, open) on site FAB-LYO, Lyon, caused by the Corporate VPN client 6.1.0 — 48 users impacted, 8 of them VIP.

items.title: Litware Insurance — 38.0% zero-touch (target 40.0%)
items.quote: 19 of 50 tickets resolved with no human touch, down from 48.0% (24 of 50) the week before.
items.note: No major incident: a surge of HR Portal access requests that no knowledge article covers, so the resolver agent hands every one to an analyst.

report.verdictIntro: Both customers breached the same 40.0% threshold, but the data alone does not tell us what Zava owes:
verdictList: Fabrikam — an outage-driven breach, on a much larger ticket volume.
Litware — a demand change, not an outage.
The contractual consequence of each breach sits in the customer contracts, not in Fabric.

choices.label: Ask ZavaIQ what the contracts say
choices.user: @ZavaIQ what do the Fabrikam and Litware contracts make us owe for this breach?
choices.assistant: The same 40.0% breach triggers two different treatments. Fabrikam's contract owes a service credit of 9,250 EUR; Litware's owes a written remediation plan by 2 October, with no credit.
choices.chain: Zava Service Desk Agent → Contracts Agent
choices.reflection:
**Fabrikam Industries — CTR-FAB-2026, XLA-FAB-01**
- "If the zero-touch resolution rate falls below 40.0% in any ISO week, Zava credits 5% of the monthly service fee for the month containing that week, within the monthly cap of 15%."
- 5% of the 185,000 EUR monthly fee = 9,250 EUR, well inside the 15% cap.

**Litware Insurance — CTR-LIT-2026, XLA-LIT-01**
- "If the zero-touch resolution rate falls below 40.0% in any ISO week, Zava delivers a written remediation plan within 10 business days. No service credit applies."
- 10 business days from the 20 September week close = 2 October.

scenarios.title: Scenario 1 — Wait for the service reviews
scenarios.body: Raise both breaches in person at the 29 September and 1 October reviews and settle them there.
scenarios.response: Waiting leaves Oliver's 22 September question unanswered for 9 days and lets the Litware remediation deadline of 2 October arrive one day after the review. The Fabrikam credit note is already drafted — holding it adds nothing. Scenario 2 settles both before the reviews.

responseSources.label: Oliver Hughes — chat with Priya Shah
Fabrikam week 38 service credit: draft ready

scenarios.title: Scenario 2 — Recommended
scenarios.body: Fabrikam: release the 9,250 EUR credit already drafted by Finance, after Head of Finance approval, and announce it at the 29 September review with the VPN rollback. Litware: no credit — Priya answers Oliver now and commits the remediation plan for 2 October (HR Portal KB article and access workflow).
scenarios.supportedBy: Supported by Fabric IQ (XLA & ontology) · Foundry IQ (contracts) · Work IQ (draft & threads) · Web IQ (announcements)

scenarios.title: Scenario 3 — Goodwill credit for both
scenarios.body: Apply a 5% credit to both customers to keep the message identical.
scenarios.response: CTR-LIT-2026 is explicit: "No service credit applies." A Litware credit would be an uncontracted concession that needs its own commercial approval, and it sets a precedent for the next breach. The contractual remedy — a remediation plan by 2 October — addresses the real cause.
